newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka grandfather called in massacre trial.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka grandfather called in massacre trial.

text.p: A 74-year-old grandfather told a Sri Lanka court how soldiers burst into his home, pointed a gun at his chest and demanded to know if they were any Tamil rebels in the village, court officials said on Thursday.

Kanapathipullai Rasiah, whose daughter was among 25 people killed in a massacre of Tamil villagers in eastern Sri Lanka last year, was giving evidence against eight soldiers charged with the atrocity, court officials said on Thursday.
Women and children were among the dead in the attack on February 11, 1996 in Trincomalee district, 240 km (150 miles) northeast of Colombo.
The soldiers have also been charged with the attempted murder of 26 civilians wounded in the attack in the village of Kumarapuram, 30 km (19 miles) south of Trincomalee, they said.
Four witnesses, out of a total of 120, gave evidence when the hearing resumed on Wednesday at Muttur, near Kumarapuram.
Rasiah told the court his daughter was killed when she went to a nearby shop.
He said he hid in his home with his grandson after they heard gunshots. Then the soldiers burst into their home, he said. The soldiers left after being told there were no rebels.

The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the mainly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island's north and east, had killed two soldiers near Kumarapuram the same day.
The government ordered an inquiry into the massacre after complaints by Tamil members of parliament.
The inquiry was deferred to June 4.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
